units.text: We'll follow a model request and decide what each safeguard can do. I A M controls whether the application can call the model. The configured guardrail evaluates supported input and output. It can intervene according to policy, but it does not grant resource access.

If an input violates the policy, the application may receive a block instead of a model answer. Output handling can block or mask according to the configured policy. Verify the behavior on the supported A P I and model; don't assume the same checks run for embedding or reranking.

CloudTrail evidence can show A P I activity, while optional invocation logs can include the actual prompt and response for supported runtime calls. Decide whether you need content rather than treating the two records as interchangeable.

If you enable invocation logs, use an eligible destination in the same account and Region and scope access appropriately. Set a retention policy. Verify which endpoint and calls are covered, and don't collect sensitive content just because the logging feature can.

The application has an identity that can invoke the service. A knowledge base has an execution role for approved stores. Neither automatically proves that the end user should get a document. Verify end-user access separately before returning retrieved information.
Configure the intended private access and key permissions where required, then test approved and denied requests. A content safeguard is not an I A M rule and can't substitute for those checks.

Pick the simplest pattern that delivers the required result. For a supported fixed task, consider the specialized service. A custom trained model fits a different requirement. A direct foundation model call works when it doesn't need private evidence; retrieval fits when the answer must be grounded in approved documents.

We'll trace a moderation decision from image to review. The service returns labels that meet your minimum confidence. Let the application decide what to flag and when a human should review an ambiguous result; no returned label is not proof the image is safe.

Record the approved review outcome and use representative test examples to check missed detections and false positives. For new designs, use an available review workflow rather than assuming Augmented AI enrollment.

Connect handles the contact and Lex gathers the intent and required input. If approved, the flow can call application logic to verify a booking. Return the answer or transfer to an agent if the request isn't understood or needs a person.

Make the fallback understandable to the caller and preserve only the context the agent needs. Restrict access to the transcript, and verify both a completed booking and a successful human handoff in testing.

Textract returns candidates for invoice fields and table cells. Validate them against the intended label and check that the totals reconcile. Being able to extract a number does not approve paying it.

Route ambiguous or inconsistent fields to authorized review. Save the approved structured record with a link to the source version. Keep permissions for source documents separate from output permissions.

We'll check what a working prototype costs and where it can run. Estimate ingestion and index maintenance, then follow each application request through the A P I, compute and model. Model input and output, storage and data transfer can have separate costs.

Verify the required model and features are offered in the approved Region. Load test typical and peak request sizes, then set budgets and limits appropriate to measured usage. Recheck eligibility and quotas before a wider rollout.

Choose by the needed result: visual moderation, clinical entity extraction, general sentiment or a grounded private answer. Verify the availability of the specific capability, not just the product name. Then test the decision using the real input type and authorized access.

We'll follow an agent from a request to a proposed action. The model can suggest the next step, but that suggestion is not permission. The application enforces policy before an approved executor can call the tool or access protected data.

Where an action carries consequences, put approval at the action boundary. Validate the caller, target and action scope before execution. A denied decision must stop the action, even if the model still proposes it.

This example shows the Agents Classic orchestration loop for eligible existing customers. It can retrieve context and use returned action results to decide what to propose next. For a new design, verify current service availability; keep the policy checks with the application regardless of orchestration product.

An action group describes operations and parameters the agent can propose. The approved executor or application validates those parameters and authorizes the action. It must reject out-of-scope requests rather than assuming the schema by itself enforces permission.

An approved executor can perform the scoped action, or the agent can return control to an application. Handle errors and retries at that boundary so a repeated proposal doesn't repeat a consequential operation.
A knowledge result is data that helps answer, not authority to use a tool. Check the caller's retrieval scope and treat the returned passage as untrusted content.

A proposed write follows a separate authorization path. Verify the supported tool, permitted parameters and any approval before calling it. If the action is denied, return a safe outcome without performing it.
